title: Enforce evidence-based LLM evaluation of task acceptance before completion
outcome: Tasks created from a plan cannot complete solely on the completing agent's assertion: an explicit acceptance-evaluation workflow assesses each authored criterion against relevant evidence, and Engram enforces the recorded decision.
acceptance: A completion attempt under an evaluated acceptance policy requires a recorded acceptance evaluation of every current authored criterion, produced by the host-orchestrated evaluator in the task's selected mode (same-session self-evaluation, host-attested sub-agent, or a separate independent session that may use a different model or provider), with access to the task outcome and relevant implementation and evidence; Engram enforces the recorded result and never calls a model itself; criteria are not silently rewritten or reduced to a fixed build/test vocabulary.

Boundary tests and documented host integration demonstrate a port-PR task with successful and failed builds plus a non-build natural-language criterion, missing evidence, stale results, and evaluator failure. Documentation clearly distinguishes LLM judgment, machine-observed evidence, and human decisions.

Completion is refused while any criterion fails, lacks sufficient evidence, or lacks an evaluation; evaluator unavailability and errors cannot silently fall back to the existing self-asserted completion path.

Each criterion receives an attributed pass, fail, or insufficient-evidence result with rationale and evidence references. Objectively executable criteria use observed check results rather than unsupported model assertions; criteria requiring human judgment surface that need.

Evaluation results are bound to the evaluated task criteria and relevant implementation/evidence state, so subsequent material changes require re-evaluation. A failed evaluation permits corrective work and another evaluation attempt.

Rollout is a per-project opt-in acceptance-evaluation policy with a revision-controlled task mode visible in show; the default preserves existing behavior, and same-session evaluated completion is recorded as distinct from the legacy self-asserted path.
